teaching.hint: Which small count for an individual bit would discard every triplicate contribution?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Each bit’s count modulo three retains only the unique value’s bit; two masks can encode the three count states for every bit in parallel.
solution_outline.approach: Scan the values with masks for count-one and count-two bits. A present input bit advances its state through zero, one, two, then zero; an absent bit leaves it unchanged. Return the count-one bit pattern.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: At each bit position, the two masks represent its count among processed values modulo three, never setting both state bits at once.
solution_outline.correctness: The three-state transition preserves the per-bit modulo count. Each triplicated value contributes three copies of its entire fixed-width pattern, cancelling at every position. The unique value contributes its one bits once, including any sign bit, so the final count-one pattern is exactly the requested signed value.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(n)` time and `O(1)` auxiliary space for fixed 32-bit values.
solution_outline.pitfall: Ordinary XOR only cancels even multiplicities. When translating the mask state transition, its second update depends on the newly updated first mask.

source_fidelity_notes: Retained exact triple/single promise, full signed value range, and mandatory linear-time/constant-space constraints.
common_wrong_turns: Ordinary XOR only cancels even multiplicities. When translating the mask state transition, its second update depends on the newly updated first mask.
